title: Lane B still spends a full-width SSH pool and a recursive NAS listing on every project every pass; CR-381's cheap half was never applied to it
what: Lane B has no SKIP/VERIFY plan and no narrow pool: each project turn spawns rclone lsf (breaker probe, own SSH login) and rclone sync with --sftp-connections 16 --checkers 16, and the + **/Proxy/** filter cannot prune any directory, so every NAS directory of the project (originals included) is listed every pass.
cost: CR-381 measured the same pool flags at 100-180 SSH logins per 27-project pass (1,600-1,950/h) for lane A. Lane B is the same order: ~1,000-1,600 logins/h, 540 rclone spawns/h and 270 recursive SFTP walks/h per idle editor at N=27 (estimated); ~20-30k logins/h at 20 machines x 30 projects.
evidence: Read: lane B always built with self.tuning; for_verify used by lane A only; CR-381 KNOWN_BUGS measurement (lane B was parked on the measured machine).
ledger: related to CR-62 (open: per-project change signal) and CR-381 (lane A only)
fix: (a) When the subpath's previous lane B outcome was NOTHING and nothing failed this pass, build lane B with tuning.for_verify() (4/4); every latch unchanged. (b) Ship the dashboard's per-project tree_sig on the selection reply and SKIP lane B when unchanged since the last clean run, with a max age after which it runs anyway; unknown signature = FULL.

title: CR-381's clean-project skip survives an untick/re-tick and a full <-> upload-only flip, so lane A skips files it has never looked at for up to 2 h
what: A clean check is keyed on subpath only. A flip to upload-only widens lane A's filter to every file (GL-13) but the old video-only 'found nothing' still yields SKIP; a project unticked, written to (notify_change cannot map it while unticked) and re-ticked also SKIPs. Neither _update_known_selection nor _prune_bookkeeping clears _lane_a_clean or _lane_a_changed_at.
cost: Non-video files of a project flipped to upload-only (its documented purpose) do not start uploading for up to lane_a_verify_seconds (7200 s) while the turn record says 'found nothing'; same for a re-ticked project. No loss (removal gate runs its own dry run); CR-383-shaped silent delay in code from 2026-11-05.
evidence: Read: _lane_a_clean is cleared only by _forget_clean_checks (resume, Sync now) and a non-clean run.
fix: Drop clean checks for slugs whose mode changed or that left/entered the selection in _update_known_selection, and prune _lane_a_clean/_lane_a_changed_at in _prune_bookkeeping; or store the filter mode in the clean-check tuple and treat a mismatch as FULL.

title: The skipped-exists alarm and the orphan .partial report hold only the LAST project scanned; tree-wide scans run N times per scan pass
what: refresh_orphan_report runs per project on the 20-turn cadence and all projects are scanned in the same pass; each call replaces the single _orphans / _size_mismatches slot, so the report ends up describing the last project only. The future-dated report was already made per-subpath for exactly this reason; these two were not. scan_trash_dir and _refresh_stray_projects (tree-wide) repeat N times in that pass.
cost: A project with re-exports that copy --ignore-existing will never upload is shown for one project-turn every ~20 passes (~2 h idle) and as 0 the rest of the time, so the SYNC-109 data-loss alarm effectively never stays up. N-1 redundant trash walks (up to 50,000 stats) and marker scans per scan pass.
ledger: related to dash-api-5 (dashboard side); companion side new
fix: Key _size_mismatches and _orphans by subpath like _future_dated_by_sub, prune to known rels, report the sum plus the per-subpath list (count stays meaningful for the current dashboard); run scan_trash_dir and _refresh_stray_projects once per pass or on their own interval.

title: Every lane C turn PATCHes the folder config even when it is already running, and reads the full Syncthing config three times per project
what: SYNC-7 removed the no-op unpause PATCH from the between-passes sweep, but the per-turn _set_paused(slug, False) remains unconditional although the turn has just fetched the folder's config (paused included). Each PATCH makes Syncthing save config.xml and broadcast ConfigSaved. The turn also GETs the whole /rest/config three times (repath per project, device ids, verify).
cost: N=27 at ~10 passes/h: ~270 config commits/h and ~810 full-config reads/h per idle editor (estimated); config.xml at 100 folders is ~100-300 KB.
evidence: Read; set_folder_paused is PATCH /rest/config/folders/<id>. Syncthing-side save cost PLAUSIBLE (from its config handler, not measured).
ledger: related to SYNC-7 (fixed for the sweep only)
fix: Return the fetched folder from _reassert_folder_policy and skip the unpause PATCH when paused is False; PATCH as today when the fetch failed. Fetch /rest/config once per turn and share it with repath's per-project check, _remote_device_ids and the verify step.

title: The Syncthing lane polls 3 + 2N REST calls every 15 s for the life of the process, including one expensive /rest/db/status per folder
what: check_once runs ping, connections, full config, then /rest/db/status and /rest/db/completion per expected folder every 15 s, unconditionally, idle or not. Syncthing documents db/status as expensive and provides the events API (FolderSummary, FolderCompletion, StateChanged, FolderErrors) for this.
cost: N=27: 57 requests per 15 s = ~13,700/h, ~330k/day per idle editor, computed by Syncthing beside Resolve; N=100: ~48,000/h (estimated cost per call).
evidence: Read; matches the SYNC-8 docstring's own '3 + 2N requests every 15 s'.
fix: Adaptive cadence: 15 s while syncing/error or after a connection change, back off to 60-120 s after two all-idle polls, reset by a sequencer turn or tray action; or a long-poll /rest/events consumer with a per-folder cache and a reconciliation poll every few minutes. Keep ping at 15 s for the supervisor, the CR-278 heal and the lane C progress token.

title: Breaker and project-dir state files are rewritten every pass when nothing changed; the breaker persists the OLDEST 512 scopes and never prunes unticked ones
what: lane_b_breaker.json is atomically rewritten twice per lane B run and project_dirs.json read and rewritten whole per lane A run regardless of change. _remote_counts (trigger 1's only memory of each scope's NAS size) is never pruned, and its persisted copy is the first 512 keys in insertion order, so once a machine has seen 512 scopes every newer project's count is memory-only and lost on restart.
cost: ~3N small file writes per pass (~810/h at N=27): small. Past 512 lifetime scopes (renames and borrowed subpaths count) a restarted machine cannot trip the 'listed as EMPTY' rule on a newer project's first pass: a commercial-scale cliff.
fix: Skip _write_state when the payload equals the last successful one (keep the failure retry); persist the newest 512 scopes or prune to the live selection; write _note_project_dir_seen at most once per project per day and prune entries unseen for 90 days.
